title: After the Fall
subtitle: How Humpty Dumpty Got Back Up Again
author: Dan Santat
description: A thoughtful, beautifully illustrated story about what happens after a famous fall—and finding the courage to try again.
about: Humpty Dumpty is famous for getting broken, but this profound Caldecott Medal-winner tells what happened next. Now terrified of heights, Humpty misses watching the birds from atop the city wall. A gentle yet empowering exploration of anxiety, healing, and the bravery it takes to face what hurt you.

storyPlot.setup: After his terrible fall from the wall, Humpty is pieced back together at the hospital—but carries deep anxiety.
storyPlot.turningPoint: He misses his passion for bird-watching and builds a paper airplane that accidentally lands back on top of the high wall.
storyPlot.resolution: Step by step, he climbs the terrifying ladder, overcomes his fear, and undergoes an astonishing transformation into something that can truly fly.

activities.title: Paper Bird Aerodynamics
activities.description: Fold a paper airplane or paper bird together. Test how small folds change how high and smoothly it glides across the room.

activities.title: The Courage Ladder
activities.description: Draw a ladder on paper. Put a small worry at the bottom rung and a brave goal at the top. Brainstorm one tiny step to take today.

cues: Why do you think Humpty felt nervous even after his shell was glued back together?
What helps you feel brave when your tummy feels fluttery?
Notice Humpty's face when he climbs the ladder—what do you think he was telling himself?

title: I Am Human
subtitle: A Book of Empathy
author: Susan Verde
description: A gentle reminder that every person has the power to choose kindness, empathy and connection.
about: A celebrated celebration of empathy and human connection. It teaches that being human means having big dreams, making mistakes, feeling imperfect, and choosing compassion and kindness each day.

storyPlot.setup: A child marvels at being born into the world with curiosity, wonder, and limitless possibilities.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Mistakes happen, words slip out that hurt others, and feelings of regret and smallness take over.
storyPlot.resolution: Recognizing that making amends, offering a hug, and practicing compassion makes us resilient and deeply connected.

portraits.name: The Young Explorer
portraits.traits: Curious, imperfect, capable of great love

portraits.name: The Companion
portraits.traits: Welcoming, forgiving, ready to hold hands

activities.title: Kindness Postcards
activities.description: Write or draw a secret note of appreciation for someone in your family or school.

activities.title: Grounding Breath
activities.description: Sit cross-legged, place a hand on your heart, and breathe in kindness, breathe out worry.

cues: What do you do when you make a mistake or hurt a friend's feelings?
How does your body feel when someone shows you unexpected kindness?
What is one kind thing we can do for someone in our neighborhood tomorrow?

title: Jabari Jumps
author: Gaia Cornwall
description: Jabari is ready to jump off the diving board. Almost. A warm story about nerves, patience and taking a brave leap.
about: Jabari has finished his swim lessons and is totally ready to jump off the diving board—almost. A tender father-son story about the patience, encouragement, and emotional safety it takes to be brave.

storyPlot.setup: Jabari declares he is ready for the tall diving board, but lets other kids go first while doing stretches.
storyPlot.turningPoint: His dad gently squeezes his hand and explains that feeling scared is just feeling ready for a surprise.
storyPlot.resolution: Jabari whispers to himself, climbs up, looks at the sky, and leaps with pure joy.

activities.title: Surprise Breath Routine
activities.description: Practice Dad's tip: take a deep breath and tell your body 'I'm ready for a surprise!'

activities.title: Splash Painting
activities.description: Use blue watercolor washes and white crayon wax-resist to paint Jabari's giant splash.

cues: Have you ever said you were ready for something when inside you felt a little butterfly in your tummy?
How did Dad help Jabari without pushing him or making him feel bad?
What is something that felt scary before you did it, but fun afterwards?

title: Lost and Found
author: Oliver Jeffers
description: A boy finds a penguin at his door and sets out across the sea to help it find its way home.
about: When a sad-looking penguin appears on a boy's doorstep, the boy assumes it is lost and rows all the way to the South Pole to return it—only to discover that what the penguin truly needed was companionship.

storyPlot.setup: A boy finds a silent penguin at his front door and tries everything to find out where it belongs.
storyPlot.turningPoint: They pack supplies, push a rowboat into the ocean, and brave stormy waves together sharing stories.
storyPlot.resolution: After leaving the penguin at the South Pole, the boy realizes the penguin wasn't lost—it was just lonely—and rows back to find his friend.

activities.title: Rowboat Storytelling
activities.description: Build a cozy blanket-fort 'rowboat' and tell each other stories under flashlight.

activities.title: Packing for an Expedition
activities.description: Draw 5 essential items you would pack to help a friend in need across the ocean.

cues: Why do you think the penguin was quiet for the whole journey?
What is the difference between being lost and feeling lonely?
How do you let your friends know that you care about them?

title: The Color Monster
subtitle: A Pop-Up Book of Feelings
author: Anna Llenas
description: A colorful introduction to naming and sorting big feelings, from happiness and sadness to calm and anger.
about: The Color Monster wakes up feeling confused, with his emotions tangled into a jumbled mess of colors. A young friend helps him untangle and sort each feeling into its own colorful jar, creating calm and clarity.

storyPlot.setup: The Color Monster is all mixed up with yellow, blue, red, grey, and green swirled together.
storyPlot.turningPoint: A little girl guides him to examine each feeling separately: yellow is joy, blue is sadness, red is anger.
storyPlot.resolution: With all feelings peacefully sorted into jars, the monster turns a rosy, gentle pink—full of love.

activities.title: Emotion Jars
activities.description: Collect clear glasses or jars. Drop yellow, blue, red, and green paper slips inside as you name your feelings today.

activities.title: Feeling Swatch Dance
activities.description: Put on upbeat music for yellow joy, slow piano for blue sadness, and stomp your feet for red anger!

cues: What color do you feel like right now?
Can you feel two different colors at the very same time? When did that happen to you?
What is something that helps you move from red (angry) back to green (calm)?

title: The Dot
author: Peter H. Reynolds
description: Vashti thinks she cannot draw, until one small mark helps her discover where creativity can begin.
about: Vashti sits with an empty paper in art class, convinced she cannot draw. Her teacher gently challenges her to 'just make a mark and see where it takes you'—sparking a transformative journey of boundless self-belief that Vashti later pays forward.

storyPlot.setup: Vashti glares at her blank paper in frustration, insisting she isn't an artist.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Her teacher asks her to make a mark and sign it, then frames it in a golden frame on the classroom wall.
storyPlot.resolution: Spurred by the framed dot, Vashti paints hundreds of colorful dots—and later encourages a younger boy who doubts his own abilities.

activities.title: One-Dot Masterpiece
activities.description: Take a sheet of paper, draw a single circle anywhere, and transform it into anything you imagine.

activities.title: Gallery Frame Signing
activities.description: Put a gold border around your child's favorite doodle and ask them to sign their artist signature.

cues: Why did the teacher frame Vashti's simple dot instead of telling her to draw something else?
How did Vashti treat the younger boy at the end of the story?
What is something creative you would love to try making this week?

title: The Heart and the Bottle
author: Oliver Jeffers
description: A poignant story about love, loss and learning that protecting your heart also means staying open to wonder.
about: A curious young girl who loved exploring the stars and the world is heartbroken by loss, so she puts her heart in a bottle to protect it. Years later, she discovers that to feel wonder and joy again, she must break it out.

storyPlot.setup: A girl and an older mentor explore questions about the ocean, stars, and curiosities of the world.
storyPlot.turningPoint: When the mentor's chair is empty, she puts her heart inside a glass bottle to stop feeling hurt, becoming dull and uninterested.
storyPlot.resolution: Meeting a little child full of questions reminds her of her lost wonder, and with the child's small hands, she frees her heart.

portraits.name: The Mentor
portraits.traits: Wise, warm, encouraging of wild questions

portraits.name: The Little Girl on the Beach

activities.title: Wonder Journal
activities.description: Keep a notebook of 3 questions about nature or the sky that no one knows the answer to yet.

activities.title: Heart of Clay
activities.description: Shape a heart out of modeling clay and talk about what makes it feel soft and warm.

cues: Why did the girl think keeping her heart in a bottle would keep it safe?
What does your heart feel like when you discover something exciting outside?
Who is someone in your life who loves answering your big questions?

title: The Invisible Boy
author: Trudy Ludwig
description: When a quiet boy is overlooked at school, one small act of friendship helps him feel seen.
about: Brian never gets picked for kickball, invited to birthday parties, or noticed by the teacher. When a new boy named Justin joins the class and gets teased, Brian reaches out with a kind drawing, opening the door to true belonging.

storyPlot.setup: Brian is drawn in black and white, unnoticed amidst the bustling, colorful classroom.
storyPlot.turningPoint: When Justin is teased for eating Korean bulgogi for lunch, Brian slips a drawing into Justin's cubby saying the food looks delicious.
storyPlot.resolution: Justin invites Brian to be his project partner; as friendship blossoms, color gradually washes over Brian until he is fully radiant.

activities.title: The Inclusion Radar
activities.description: Notice one person at the playground or park who is sitting alone, and invite them to play tag or share a smile.

activities.title: Black & White to Color Sketch
activities.description: Draw someone in pencil, then add bursts of vibrant color when they feel happy and included.

cues: Have you ever felt like Brian, where you felt quiet or left out?
How did Brian's small drawing change Justin's whole day—and his own?
What is something welcoming we can say to someone new in class?

title: The Magical Yet
author: Angela DiTerlizzi
description: A lyrical celebration of the little word that keeps us learning: yet.
about: When learning to ride a bike ends in a scrape and tears, a glowing magical creature called 'The Yet' appears to show that not being able to do something is just a temporary state on the road to mastery.

storyPlot.setup: A child falls off a bike and wants to throw it away forever in frustration.
storyPlot.turningPoint: The Magical Yet appears, showing flashbacks of when the child couldn't walk, babble, or tie shoes either.
storyPlot.resolution: With practice, laughter, and patience, the child learns that mistakes are stepping stones to mastering any skill.

activities.title: The 'Not Yet' Jar
activities.description: Write down 3 things you can't do yet (e.g. whistle, cartwheel) and tape the word YET in big gold letters.

activities.title: Practice Chart
activities.description: Choose one tiny skill and practice for 3 minutes a day for a week.

cues: What is something you couldn't do last year that you can easily do now?
What can you say to yourself the next time something feels too hard to finish?
How does the word 'yet' change the way a sentence feels?

title: The Rabbit Listened
author: Cori Doerrfeld
description: When Taylor is upset, the animals offer advice—but the rabbit knows that sometimes the best help is simply listening.
about: When Taylor's magnificent block tower crashes, different animal friends rush in telling Taylor how to react. Only the rabbit sits quietly, leans in, and offers the warm gift of presence.

storyPlot.setup: Taylor builds a majestic block tower, but a flock of birds knocks it down into ruins.
storyPlot.turningPoint: The chicken squawks to talk, the bear wants to roar, the snake wants to knock down other towers—none of which helps.
storyPlot.resolution: The rabbit inches closer, sits silently until Taylor is ready to cry, talk, roar, and finally rebuild together.

activities.title: The Rabbit Blanket Hug
activities.description: Wrap up in a cozy blanket and practice 'listening like a rabbit' without giving any advice for 2 whole minutes.

activities.title: Block Tower Challenge
activities.description: Build the tallest tower you can, take a photo, and gently knock it down with a laugh.

cues: When you are upset, do you prefer people to talk a lot, or do you prefer a quiet hug like the rabbit?
How can you be a 'rabbit' for your friend when they are having a rough day?
Why didn't the other animals' advice help Taylor right away?

title: The Wonderful Things You Will Be
author: Emily Winfield Martin
description: A warm, rhyming celebration of the many wonderful ways a child can grow into themselves.
about: A rhythmic, poetic ode to the boundless kindness, curiosity, and creativity that children carry inside them as they grow up into who they are meant to be.

storyPlot.setup: A parent looks at their child and wonders who this small, bright person will become.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Exploring possibilities not just of careers, but of character: being kind, helping someone in the rain, being brave in dark forests.
storyPlot.resolution: The promise that whatever path they take, their goodness, curiosity, and love will always be cherished.

activities.title: Time Capsule Wish
activities.description: Draw a picture of your dream treehouse, animal friend, or future self, and seal it in an envelope to open next birthday.

activities.title: Tree of Kindness
activities.description: Cut out paper leaves and write on each leaf one kind thing your child did this week.

cues: What is something you love doing that makes you feel most like yourself?
What kind of helper do you want to be in our neighborhood?
What is your favorite way to make someone smile?

title: When Sadness Is at Your Door
author: Eva Eland
description: A quiet, reassuring book that gives sadness a shape—and shows children how to make room for it.
about: Sadness often arrives uninvited and feels overwhelming. This soothing guide personifies Sadness as a gentle visitor to sit with, drink tea with, and take on a quiet walk until it is ready to move on.

storyPlot.setup: Sadness knocks on the door looking like a heavy, gentle grey cloud that won't go away.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Instead of pushing it into a closet or running away, you give it a name, sit beside it, and draw together.
storyPlot.resolution: After sharing cocoa, listening to music, and going for a quiet walk, Sadness gently packs its bags and moves along.

portraits.name: The Host
portraits.traits: Brave enough to welcome tough feelings

activities.title: Tea Party with Sadness
activities.description: Pour two imaginary cups of warm tea. Ask: 'What are you trying to tell me today?'

activities.title: Quiet Nature Walk
activities.description: Walk outside without talking, collecting 3 smooth stones or autumn leaves.

cues: What does sadness look or feel like in your chest or tummy?
Why does trying to hide sadness make it feel heavier instead of lighter?
What helps you feel cozy and supported when you are having a down day?

title: You Choose
author: Pippa Goodhart
description: A playful picture book full of possibilities, inviting children to imagine the people, places and lives they might choose.
about: An endlessly re-readable picture book where every page offers dozens of delightful choices: where to live, what to eat, what to travel in, and who to bring along on adventures.

storyPlot.setup: Open the cover to enter an imaginative sandbox where you decide every detail of your universe.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Comparing wild choices—from living in a treehouse to sailing in a submarine, eating spicy curry or moon cake.
storyPlot.resolution: Discovering that your friend's choices are completely different from yours, making conversation and sharing rich.

activities.title: Dream House Blueprint
activities.description: Grab a big sheet of paper and draw your ultimate room with slides, book nooks, and secret tunnels.

activities.title: 'Would You Rather' Dinner Game
activities.description: Take turns asking silly questions around the dinner table.

cues: If you could pick any vehicle on this page to take us to school tomorrow, which would you pick and why?
If your best friend picked a completely different bed than you, how could you compromise?
Which meal on the food spread would you cook for our family tonight?

title: The Most Magnificent Thing
author: Ashley Spires
description: A girl and her dog discover that making something magnificent takes patience, perspective and room for a few wrong turns.
about: A girl knows exactly how her magnificent invention will look and work. But making it proves frustrating, and she gets mad—until a walk with her dog clears her head and helps her see mistakes as clues.

storyPlot.setup: The girl gathers scrap parts, cardboard, and tools to build something magnificent for her dog.
storyPlot.turningPoint: Every prototype is wrong, crooked, or broken; she gets furious, smashes parts, and wants to quit.
storyPlot.resolution: Her dog insists on a walk. Breathing in fresh air, she spots good parts on previous failures and assembles the true magnificent scooter.

portraits.name: The Canine Assistant
portraits.traits: Enthusiastic, patient, always up for a walk

activities.title: The Junk Drawer Challenge
activities.description: Collect cardboard rolls, bottle caps, and tape. Build a prototype of an imaginary machine!

activities.title: The Frustration Reset Walk
activities.description: Practice stepping outside and naming 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, and 3 you can hear.

cues: What happened to the girl's hands and face when she got super angry?
How did going for a walk help her brain come up with better ideas?
What is something you worked hard on that didn't work the first time?

title: The Bad Seed
author: Jory John
description: A sunflower seed with a bad reputation decides to change, one honest and hopeful step at a time.
about: A sunflower seed with a notorious reputation for bad manners and grumpy faces decides it's tired of being bad, showing that anyone can choose to start fresh with kindness, gratitude, and second chances.

storyPlot.setup: The Bad Seed boasts about cutting in line, never washing his hands, and glaring at everyone.
storyPlot.turningPoint: He shares his backstory—he was part of a happy sunflower family until getting harvested, bagged, and nearly eaten at a baseball game.
storyPlot.resolution: He takes a deep breath and decides that even though it's hard, he will say please, smile, and try to be good.

activities.title: Seed of Kindness Badge
activities.description: Draw a little seed badge with a smiley face and wear it whenever you do a good deed.

activities.title: Second Chances Roleplay
activities.description: Practice what to say when you feel like being grumpy vs choosing a polite word.

cues: Why did the Bad Seed start acting so grumpy in the first place?
Does deciding to be kind mean you will never have a bad day again?
How does it feel when someone gives you a second chance after a mistake?
